prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 96-120 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a living whirlwind: a tall spinning column of pale grey-white and pale teal wind bands with crisp dark outlines, wider at the top and narrowing to a twisting point below, two arms of swirling wind, a stern face formed from the wind bands near the top (two hollow eyes and a frowning mouth), a few small brown rocks and leaves caught inside the swirl and drawn within the wind, none flying loose; it hovers, nothing touches the ground; centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: a stern face formed from the wind itself (two hollow eyes and a frowning mouth), no skin.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, the column leaning toward the heroes, both wind arms reaching out with the elbows bent so they stay well inside the middle cell, the swirl spinning tighter, facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the column bent and fraying at the top, the arms thrown up, the same pale grey-white and teal colours as in the idle cell, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Keep the figure upright and level in every cell. The idle cell shows it at its lowest; in the attack and the hurt it rises a little, so its lowest point is clearly higher than in the idle cell, with more empty space below it: in the attack it leans its top and wind arms toward the heroes; in the hurt it is knocked back up and to the left and tilted back by about fifteen degrees; it always hovers, nothing touches the ground; the swirl moves with the motion, every streak attached to the body. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, hovering above the ground, nothing touches the ground, no shadow, no water. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, skin, legs, a body, water, fire, separate rocks flying, loose streaks, lightning, a ground cloud, dust.
